observation.visible_scene: A low-angle daytime view of a bright blue sky. The sun sits high near the top-center, producing a strong glare and fixed lens-flare artifacts (a rainbow streak below it and a faint circle at upper right). Scattered white cumulus and wispy clouds fill the sky. Along the bottom edge a dark silhouette of tree tops and a house roof with a chimney and antenna remain in view.
visible_changes: The foreground (trees, roof, chimney, antenna) stays in the same pixel positions throughout, indicating the camera is essentially static.
The sun and the lens-flare artifacts remain fixed in position relative to the frame, consistent with a stationary camera pointed at the same sky region.
The cloud on the left edge drifts slowly rightward across the sequence (its left boundary moves from off-frame at the start to roughly the left-center by the end).
A puffy cloud in the upper-right corner gradually enters and enlarges within the frame from about the middle of the clip onward.
The mid-right cloud cluster shifts slightly right and downward over time.
The horizontal wispy cloud band in the lower-middle stretches/changes shape modestly but does not translate dramatically.
A few tiny dark specks appear at isolated positions in some frames (e.g., left sky, lower sky), possibly birds, but their motion is not traceable.
outside_clip_unknowns: The actual wind speed and direction driving the cloud drift is not visible.
Whether the small dark specks are birds, insects, or sensor dust cannot be determined from these frames.
Any camera motion outside this cropped window (the segment may begin or end mid-pan) is unknown.
uncertain_details: The apparent rightward cloud motion could be partly a very slow camera pan, though the unchanged foreground and sun make a static camera more likely.
The exact trajectory of the tiny specks is too sparse to confirm as a single moving object.
